current.text: Billy Donovan, who pulled him early and kept him on a short leash, is gone. Tiago Splitter is the new Bulls head coach.

Coby White and Nikola Vucevic are gone. Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson have arrived. The projected starting five is Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Buzelis, Caleb Wilson and Nick Claxton. With Claxton at center and Wilson at the four, Buzelis plays out of position at the three.

After last season's trade deadline he ranked 50th. In 31 minutes with 25% usage he averaged 19 points, 7 rebounds, 3 threes, almost 2 blocks and a steal. Over the final 20 games he played 33 to 34 minutes.
Experts expect a big third-year step, with about 32 minutes and more shots. His usage should land between his season-long 22 and his late-season 25.

Experts disagree on where he sits in the Bulls usage order. Some see him as the first or second option, ahead of Giddey and Caleb Wilson. Another expects Norman Powell to lead the team in usage unless Powell is traded.
Splitter is expected to give him more ball handling and point forward duties, so his assists should rise. How much Splitter will empower him is still an open question.
Several experts expect his blocks to drop this season because he will play more small forward next to Caleb Wilson.
Experts see him as a top 50 player in category and points leagues, probably ranked around 44 to 51. They call his Yahoo rank too low and say he still offers a lot of value.
He is the best fantasy target on the Bulls. Do not take him around pick 40. Around pick 60 is good value, and around 80 would be a steal.
He went for 22 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
His fair auction price is about 20 USD. Josh is a big fan but would only pay up to his value.

The Bulls project as a bad team, probably bottom ten in the league, with about 32 wins. They played at a very fast pace late last season and should keep an up-tempo style. The front office signs veterans and hopes to trade them.
The Bulls play 3-3-4 games (10 in total) in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 with the March 28 end. They have 15 back-to-backs, one below the league maximum.

durable.text: Blocks are his standout category. His projected 1.6 per game is far above the pool, even more so for a forward.
He makes many threes for a forward, but his three-point percentage is low. He shot 35% from three last season and 32% after the trade deadline.
None of his categories is clearly weak, so he fits any build.

note: Experts agree he is a top 50 player. The market is lower: Yahoo rank 69, Yahoo average cost 9.0 USD and ESPN average cost 4.2 USD. He went for 12 USD in our league last season, but expect our managers to pay closer to the experts' fair price of about 20 USD (22 USD in a recent mock), so anything under 20 USD is a buy. His elite blocks and threes from a forward, with no weak category, fit any build. Early in the season, check whether Splitter gives him about 32 minutes, whether he stays ahead of Powell in usage, and whether his blocks hold at small forward.
